title: Quantum Channel Polynomial Processing
authors: Tianhan Liu, Fedor Simkovic, Martin Leib
abstract: We introduce a quantum algorithmic framework based on probabilistic mixtures of unitary channels that, similar to the framework of quantum singular value transformations, enables the application of arbitrary polynomials of hermitian operators onto arbitrary initial states. We show that our framework supports a flexible tradeoff between sample- and query complexity ranging from optimal query complexity, meaning logarithmic in the error, and exponentially scaling sample complexity to sub-polynomial query complexity in the error and polynomial sample complexity. Combined with the considerably lower quantum circuit complexity, compared to quantum singular value transformations with a linear combination of unitaries block encoding, we argue that our framework can be seamlessly scaled from NISQ to fault-tolerant quantum computing.
summary: The paper introduces Quantum Channel Polynomial Processing (QCPP), an algorithm designed to implement functions of Hermitian operators on quantum states. By replacing complex coherent unitaries with stochastic probabilistic mixtures, QCPP significantly simplifies the circuit requirements compared to existing techniques like QSVT. This advancement makes simulating complex Hamiltonians more feasible for near-term and intermediate-scale quantum hardware.
main_problem: Developing a quantum algorithmic framework to efficiently apply arbitrary functions of Hermitian operators, $f(H)ho f(H)^\dagger$, on an initial quantum state.
main_result: The proposed Quantum Channel Polynomial Processing (QCPP) method achieves a favorable tradeoff between sample and query complexity, allowing for polynomial sample scaling with respect to the required precision.
method: QCPP replaces coherent block encoding used in QSVT with stochastic encodings of Hamiltonian commutators/anti-commutators at the channel level, utilizing probabilistic mixtures of unitary channels.
model_or_system: The framework operates on an n-qubit computational register and one ancillary qubit. The target process approximates applying a function $f$ to a Hermitian operator $H$, which is constructed from Pauli operators.
key_observables: Sample Complexity ($\Gamma(p)$), Query Complexity ($d$), and the resulting quantum channel $\mathcal{F}$.
important_parameters: The tradeoff between sample complexity (related to polynomial coefficients) and query complexity (number of basic blocks $d$).
main_assumptions: It assumes the ability to implement the probabilistic building block $E$, and it relies on polynomial interpolation techniques for approximating the target function $f$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the workflow: polynomial interpolation, construction of the basic computational building block via stochastic sampling, concatenation of blocks corresponding to roots, and the final measurement sequence.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the problem (applying $f(H)$) to introducing QCPP as a replacement for QSVT's coherent encoding. It details the mathematical structure using probabilistic mixtures and analyzes the resulting complexity trade-offs by constructing specific polynomials that yield polynomial sample scaling.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses algorithmic efficiency in quantum simulation, offering a hardware-friendly alternative to complex unitary encodings required by standard QSVT methods for simulating Hamiltonians relevant to AMO physics.
